clue.text: Start to jostle one holding milk shake

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of jostle is used

parts.note: a cow's udder is the organ that holds milk

explanation.surface: Someone is jostled while carrying a milkshake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk shake' looks like one drink, but 'milk' belongs to the udder and 'shake' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To judder is to shake or vibrate violently, a direct synonym.

clue.text: BBC from 4th of January is free

indicators.note: the nickname is read only from its letter U onwards, U being the fourth letter of the word January, so its opening letter falls away

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The BBC is free of charge from the fourth of January.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE, read from its U (the 4th letter of 'January') onwards, loses its first letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to set it free, as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tied into arrangement, having to include unknown composer

indicators.note: these words say one piece must be placed inside the other
an arrangement of the letters puts them in a new order

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so Z here

explanation.surface: Someone is tied into a musical arrangement involving an unknown composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into arrangement' puts TIEDINTO into a new order, and the Z goes inside it to give the Italian opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was an Italian composer of operas such as Lucia di Lammermoor.

clue.text: Hood good as clothing

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend

explanation.surface: A hood is as good as clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is not a garment but the legendary outlaw's surname, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Robing means dressing or putting on clothes, especially ceremonial robes, so it can mean clothing as a verb form.

clue.text: Upset after budget limit is measured

parts.note: a cap is a limit placed on spending
to size something is to measure it

explanation.surface: Someone is upset after their budget limit is set.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is upset has overturned, which is what capsized means.

clue.text: Fine in school holiday to take quick early course

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school
OK means fine or all right
a school holiday is a break
fast means quick

explanation.surface: During the school holidays someone takes a quick early course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early course' sounds academic, but it is the first meal of the day as a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried morning meal is the first course of the day, eaten early.

clue.text: Excellent spectacles might make one this

explanation.surface: Good glasses could make someone outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as PEER LESS: with spectacles you squint less.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, so excellent; and wearing glasses means you need to peer less.

clue.text: Current affairs on a holiday island

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
biz is slang for business, affairs

explanation.surface: Current affairs are being discussed on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current affairs' reads as news, but splits into a physics symbol and a business word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a holiday resort.

clue.text: Watch dog making application to viewers

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
to dog someone is to follow them, to shadow them

explanation.surface: A guard dog is used for viewers' benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' are eyes, so the make-up is applied to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up applied to the eyelids is put onto the eyes, the body's viewers.

clue.text: Hard negotiator never finishes penniless

parts.note: stony means hard

indicators.note: the word is left without its finish, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a broker negotiates deals for others

explanation.surface: A tough negotiator never completes a deal and is left broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony-broke is British slang for having no money at all.

clue.text: Cold start of last month recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: the first of December, the last month of the year, written DEC I with the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It was cold at the beginning of last month, someone remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last month' is not the previous month but December, the year's last; its start is the 1st, DEC I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means frozen or chilled, so very cold.

clue.text: No end peculiar, being arrested by coppers in pirates' home

indicators.note: being held by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pence

indicators.note: the word loses its end, its last letter

parts.note: zany means peculiar or eccentric

explanation.surface: Something peculiar has been arrested by the police in a pirates' hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but means low-value coins. Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera is The Pirates of Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: Penzance, a Cornish seaside town, is home to the pirates in the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.

clue.text: A hotel under construction cannot stand

indicators.note: being built, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hotel being built is something people dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to detest it, which is to be unable to stand it.

clue.text: Call for attention from vessel in training

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: PT is physical training
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A call comes from a ship on a training exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed sound made to catch someone's attention quietly.

clue.text: Caught with unusual item in kitchen?

parts.note: snared means caught in a trap
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: Someone is caught with a strange object in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitchen' is orchestral slang for the percussion section, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum belongs to the percussion section, nicknamed the kitchen in orchestras.

clue.text: Working with association bringing butter in

parts.note: busy means working, occupied
a body is an organised group or association

explanation.surface: A dairy group is working on bringing butter in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts in.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler who interferes is someone who butts in, a butter-in.

clue.text: Building ablaze in park finally split into sections

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together anew
the final letter of park is used

explanation.surface: A building blazing in a park finally breaks apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like a noun, but signals that ABLAZE, IN and K are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To balkanize a region is to divide it into small hostile sections, as the Balkans were.

clue.text: Scots beef when pass goes in not straight

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: gay as the opposite of straight
to pass a measure is to allow it

explanation.surface: Scottish beef is approved when it passes, though not straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloway is a breed of beef cattle from south-west Scotland.

clue.text: One thousand in shock following king's suicide

indicators.note: the rest comes after the king's letter

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to amaze is to shock or astonish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thousand people were shocked after the king took his own life.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamikaze were Japanese suicide pilots, so the word means suicidal, a suicide mission.

clue.text: Wife wearing light blue

indicators.note: the wife has the other piece on her, around her, so it encloses her

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: A wife is wearing pale blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light blue' reads as a colour, but 'light' is fodder and 'blue' means risque.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of risque or smutty, as in blue jokes, means lewd.

clue.text: Bush may rot and lie hollow

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving each word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shrub may rot and lie empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: What sailors are to boat here

definitions.text: What sailors are to boat here

indicators.note: in this word, meaning the sailors sit within the boat

parts.note: keel is a word for a boat, especially a flat-bottomed barge
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the role sailors play on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a kernel is a core, and here the sailors form the core of the boat word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the central part or core, which is what the sailors are inside the boat word.

clue.text: Trapeze artist daring to perform with this group?

definitions.text: Trapeze artist daring to perform with this

explanation.surface: A brave trapeze artist performs with a troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as NO NET: what a daring trapeze artist works without.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians; a daredevil performer works with no safety net.

clue.text: Principal slowly emerging in film

parts.note: key means principal or chief
largo is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: A principal is slowly emerging in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Key Largo is a 1948 film starring Humphrey Bogart and Lauren Bacall.

clue.text: In which air's sucked in quietly? Yes and no

definitions.text: In which air's sucked in quietly? Yes and no

indicators.note: drawn inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: air is taken as gas, with the possessive s kept as a letter
p is the musical marking piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A question about breathing in softly, answered both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no': these intakes of breath do suck in air, but not quietly; meanwhile the wordplay puts P inside GAS'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasps are sharp intakes of breath, the air sucked in suddenly.

clue.text: The country's good for one elderly relative

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: Iran is a country
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The country's good for an elderly relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran is a familiar word for grandmother, an elderly relative.

clue.text: Seat with short leg strangely is most comfortable

indicators.note: the letters are put in a strange new order
cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A chair with a short leg is oddly the most comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'comfortable' here means well off, not cosy, which is why the definition misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The richest are financially comfortable, comfortable meaning well off.

clue.text: In a year's time opera house to take on hard rock

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Y abbreviates year, with the possessive s kept
the Met is the Metropolitan Opera House in New York
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: In a year an opera house will take on hard rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take on' joins the opera house and hard as one piece; 'rock' is a gemstone mineral, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz, a semi-precious rock.

clue.text: Making comeback pros never box however

indicators.note: Making comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
to box is to enclose, so the words contain the answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Professionals never make a comeback in boxing, however.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'box however' as the definition, but 'box' is the containment signal: the words enclose the letters. Only 'however' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is a phrase meaning nevertheless, however.
